The ferry timetable nobody can read

The new ferry timetable for the estuary runs to eleven pages, uses four colours and three kinds of footnote, and has already been printed twice because the first run left out the Sunday sailings.

Passengers at the north slipway say they now ask the crew rather than read the board. The operator says a simpler version is on its way, and that the colours were meant to make the tide-dependent sailings easier to spot.

A spokesperson added that the footnotes would be cut from three kinds to one, and that the next printing would be checked against the old timetable line by line before it went to the slipways.

Regular passengers have started a noticeboard of their own beside the ticket hut, with the week's sailings written out by hand in a single colour.
